extracted.intended_audience: researchers (authors and reviewers) in the life and biomedical sciences considering submitting to or reviewing for eLife
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational guidelines describing eLife's peer review policies and expectations for editors, reviewers and authors in the life and biomedical sciences, including transparency, decision-making, and requests for additional experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access to peer review reports and editors' assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone can read the peer review reports and editors' assessment for all published eLife papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects a commitment to transparency so that the assessment of expert reviewers is visible to authors, readers and other interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish decision letter and authors' response
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision letter sent to the author after peer review, and the authors' response to this letter, are published with accepted manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing both the decision letter and the authors' response increases openness about the editorial process and how concerns raised during review were addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor qualifications — active researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions are made by editors who are active researchers in the life and biomedical sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decision-making is vested in practitioners with current subject-matter expertise to ensure informed judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial limits on publication volume or acceptance rate
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not artificially limit the number of articles we publish or have a set acceptance rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance decisions are driven by quality and fit, not by maintaining a target acceptance percentage or quota.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultative review — editors and reviewers discuss before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers discuss their reviews with each other before reaching a decision on a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This collaborative discussion is intended to produce a more considered and consistent editorial decision than isolated reviews alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit requests for additional experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra experiments are only requested if they are essential and can be completed within about two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy aims to make peer review faster by reducing rounds of revision and avoiding burdensome or non-essential experimental demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall aims: faster, fairer, more open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall aim is to make peer review faster (by reducing rounds of revision and only requesting extra experiments when they are essential), fairer and more open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These priorities guide editorial choices about whether to request more work, how to run discussions, and what to publish alongside articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject use of Journal Impact Factor for assessment; support DORA
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not support the Impact Factor and is a co-founder of the Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife instead envisions assessment systems that emphasize the outputs of peer review and research quality rather than journal title or impact-factor metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision: assess research by peer-review outputs rather than journal title
rubrics_metrics.description: In the future we envision a system in which the outputs of peer review are the primary way research is assessed, rather than journal title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This strategic vision shapes current policies toward transparency and publishing review materials so that assessments of work are visible and portable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly available editorial-process metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly updated metrics relating to the eLife editorial process are available in our Author Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife makes metrics about its editorial process accessible to authors and the community to support accountability and continuous improvement.
